harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored tickets.sql into PostgreSQL database helpdesk and repaired automatic ID allocation. Original tickets remain unchanged; post-restart automatic inserts received IDs above 100. The source export, RHEL 10.0 release, kernel, SELinux, and firewalld were preserved. Node1 was safely rebooted and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 16.15 from the signed RHEL 10 repository without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Initialized and enabled the stock PostgreSQL service with its loopback-only listener.
Reproduced the pre-repair duplicate-ID failure, then transactionally aligned tickets_id_seq with imported maximum ID 100.
Verified automatic allocation before and after reboot using rolled-back inserts; IDs 101 and 102 were allocated, leaving no test rows.
Safely rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed, PostgreSQL recovered, and all data persisted.

evidence.summary: The export created the table and inserted three rows; final proof identifies database=helpdesk and the SERIAL default.

evidence.requirement: Preserve existing ticket IDs and text.
evidence.summary: Final stored data remains exactly 1:Printer queue, 2:Scanner cable, and 100:Office move, with three rows total.

evidence.requirement: New omitted-ID tickets receive unique IDs above the imported maximum.
evidence.summary: The original collision at ID 1 was reproduced; sequence repair set it to 100; automatic probes allocated IDs 101 and, after reboot, 102. Both probes were rolled back.
tickets.sql remains root-owned at the requested path with unchanged size and SHA-256 5a9b51de0c539f9ffedd0ca1424be6549bbef62a5414b6545d879d9c1be973c5.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software.
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged; PostgreSQL 16.15 was installed from the RHEL 10 AppStream repository.

Healthy baseline boot ID 24d7af09-d9dc-453c-9bbd-d48f7dc4eb4e was captured, the native safe reboot was acknowledged, and boot ID changed to 1399e1cc-f2b9-4645-9d28-3b6e33c53d21. PostgreSQL returned enabled, active, and accepting connections; data, sequence behavior, source checksum, SELinux enforcing state, and firewalld all recovered with zero failed units.
